subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept the scoped unified-exec native PreToolUse path for policy-active Codex turns once `code_mode_exec` is normalized, given the Codex runtime prerequisite and session-binding compatibility tradeoff?
rationale: This changes a tool-execution security boundary and upgrade behavior; automation can repair the missing alias, but it cannot decide whether this Codex runtime dependency and fresh-thread behavior are the intended product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Accept after normalization
options.body: Land the scoped positive-delivery path after `code_mode_exec` is routed through the established `exec` policy surface and focused regression coverage is added.

options.title: Pause for runtime proof
options.body: Hold the PR until current packaged Codex behavior and version pinning prove the same native PreToolUse delivery without relying on a local patched runtime assumption.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed alternative
options.body: Use #90805 or #90633 as the canonical direction if maintainers prefer disabling or failing closed over relying on positive Codex hook delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept after normalization
recommendation.body: Land the scoped positive-delivery path after `code_mode_exec` is routed through the established `exec` policy surface and focused regression coverage is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent native hook relay and Codex runtime work makes this the strongest available maintainer-side decision owner signal among the history candidates.
